title: Random Variables
description: Understand random variables, sample spaces, discrete and continuous variables, probability mass functions, probability density functions, and cumulative distribution functions.
learningObjectives: Explain experiments, outcomes, and sample spaces.
Define random variables and distinguish them from ordinary variables.
Differentiate discrete and continuous random variables.
Understand probability mass and density functions.
Connect random variables to uncertainty in machine learning.

content.title: Random Experiment
content.body: A random experiment is a process whose exact outcome is uncertain before it occurs. Examples include tossing a coin, rolling a die, or randomly selecting a data point.

content.title: Sample Space
content.body: The sample space is the set of all possible outcomes of a random experiment.

content.title: Rolling a Die
content.problem: What is the sample space when rolling a fair six-sided die?
solution: A standard die has six possible outcomes.
Each outcome is an integer from 1 to 6.

content.title: Definition
content.body: A random variable is a function that assigns a numerical value to each outcome in a random experiment. It allows uncertain outcomes to be studied using mathematics.

content.title: Why Random Variables Matter
content.body: Random variables provide a mathematical way to describe uncertain quantities such as customer purchases, measurement errors, image classifications, and model predictions.

content.title: Number of Heads
content.problem: A fair coin is tossed twice. Let X be the number of heads. What values can X take?
solution: The possible outcomes are HH, HT, TH, and TT.
HT and TH each contain one head.
content.answer: X can take the values 0, 1, and 2.

content.title: Definition
content.body: A discrete random variable takes values from a finite or countably infinite set. Examples include the number of customers arriving in an hour and the number of defective products in a batch.

content.title: Probability Mass Function
content.body: A probability mass function, or PMF, assigns a probability to each possible value of a discrete random variable.

content.title: A Discrete Probability Distribution
content.problem: A random variable X takes values 0, 1, and 2 with probabilities 0.2, 0.5, and 0.3. Is this a valid PMF?
content.answer: Yes, it is a valid PMF.

content.title: Definition
content.body: A continuous random variable can take values over a continuum, such as a range of real numbers. Examples include time, height, temperature, and measurement errors.

content.title: Probability Density Function
content.body: A probability density function, or PDF, describes the density of probability across possible values. Probabilities over intervals are found by integrating the density.

content.title: PDF Conditions
content.body: f(x) >= 0; integral over all x of f(x) dx = 1

content.title: Probability at One Exact Value
content.body: For a continuous random variable with a density, the probability of taking any one exact value is zero. Probabilities are calculated over intervals.

content.title: Uniform Distribution
content.problem: Let X be uniformly distributed on the interval [0, 1]. What is P(0.2 <= X <= 0.5)?
solution: The probability equals the interval length multiplied by the density.

content.title: Definition
content.body: The cumulative distribution function, or CDF, gives the probability that a random variable is less than or equal to a specified value.

content.title: Important Properties
content.body: A CDF is nondecreasing, approaches zero toward negative infinity, and approaches one toward positive infinity. It is right-continuous.

content.title: Calculate a Cumulative Probability
content.problem: Suppose X takes values 1, 2, and 3 with probabilities 0.2, 0.5, and 0.3. Find F(2).

sections.title: Random Variables in AI and Machine Learning

content.title: Modeling Uncertainty
content.body: Random variables are used to describe uncertain observations, model outputs, labels, sampling processes, and measurement errors.

content.title: Classification Example
content.body: A binary classification label can be represented by a random variable Y that takes values 0 and 1. A probabilistic classifier may estimate P(Y = 1 given an input X).

content.title: Simulating a Random Variable with Python
content.body:
import numpy as np

rng = np.random.default_rng(42)

# Simulate 10,000 fair coin tosses.
tosses = rng.binomial(n=1, p=0.5, size=10000)

# Let X be the number of heads in two tosses.
pairs = tosses[:10000 - 1].reshape(-1)  # Individual toss outcomes

print('Estimated probability of heads:', tosses.mean())
content.explanation: A Bernoulli random variable represents a single trial with outcomes 0 and 1. The sample mean estimates the probability of obtaining 1. The random seed makes the simulation reproducible.

exercises.question: What is a random variable?
options: A function that assigns numerical values to outcomes
A probability that must equal zero
A function that always returns one
exercises.correctAnswer: A function that assigns numerical values to outcomes
exercises.solution: A random variable maps outcomes of a random experiment to numerical values.

exercises.question: Which is an example of a discrete random variable?
options: The exact height of a randomly selected person
The time taken to finish a task
The number of defective items in a batch
The temperature at a particular moment
exercises.correctAnswer: The number of defective items in a batch
exercises.solution: The number of defective items is countable and takes integer values.

exercises.question: A random variable takes values 0 and 1 with probabilities 0.4 and 0.6. What is the probability that it equals 1?
A random variable takes values 1, 2, and 3 with probabilities 0.1, 0.6, and 0.3. Calculate P(X <= 2).
For a continuous random variable with a probability density, what is P(X = a) for a single exact value a?
exercises.solution: A single point has zero probability under a continuous distribution with a density.

summary: A random variable assigns numerical values to random outcomes.
Discrete random variables use probability mass functions.
Continuous random variables use probability density functions.
Random variables provide the foundation for probabilistic modeling in AI.
